source.title: Unleashing the Potential of Regularization Strategies in Learning with Noisy Labels
source.authors: Hui-Sung Kang; Sheng Liu; Huaxi Huang; Jun Yu; Bo Han; Dadong Wang; Tong-Liang Liu

record.tranche_reason: Tests performance on datasets with synthetic label corruption, using test accuracy across noise levels. It does not measure training error or use completely random labels.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracy for RegCE across synthetic noise conditions. It does not report training error on these conditions. Results cited from other papers and results comparing methods are not extracted as this study’s own tests of the claim.
record.test_reason: Section 3.1 and Figure 2(b) report the study's own clean-versus-noisy training-loss trajectories, directly bearing on V6. The record incorrectly says no such comparison is reported. Most other experiments evaluate the proposed mitigation method's test accuracy.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that cross-entropy combined with sharp learning-rate decay, weak and strong augmentation, and EMA weight averaging can match or outperform specialized noisy-label methods, with further gains from semi-supervised learning.
record.recipe_differences: Uses synthetic partial label corruption and RegCE’s combined regularization strategy; does not use completely random labels or measure training error as in the original studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise type and fraction; dataset; use of semi-supervised learning. The study also reports sensitivity to learning-rate decay settings and EMA momentum.

fits_no_version.finding: RegCE and RegCE+semi achieve strong test accuracy under synthetic and real-world label noise; ablations compare regularization strategies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Combined learning-rate scheduling, augmentation, and weight averaging improve generalization under label noise.

record.problems: No training-error results are reported for the synthetic label-noise experiments, so the study cannot establish whether the models fit the corrupted training labels. Noise levels do not span none to all.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted: reported results are test accuracies under partial synthetic label corruption, without training-error measurements. Those test-accuracy values alone do not establish the training-set fitting behavior V4 specifies. Tables 1 and 2 report the results by method, dataset, and noise level; no result meeting the row criterion is available for V4.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged training hyperparameters.
Training time relative to true labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training-set fit across corruption fractions and degradation over the full zero-to-total-corruption range. Test accuracy under partial corruption alone does not establish this combined claim.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent fitting completely random labels, and generalization on true labels after removing regularization.

Eventual memorization of noisy labels after initial clean-pattern learning is not established by the reported large-learning-rate comparison; precise learning-order differences at the small learning rate are not stated.

missing.what: Clean- and noisy-sample training-loss trajectories at constant learning rate 0.1: clean loss decreases while noisy loss remains high. Add condition-specific rows using the stated qualitative result; exact curve values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

Clean- and noisy-sample training-loss trajectories at constant learning rate 0.001. The caption reports faster noise fitting under the small learning rate, but does not establish that noise is learned before clean labels. Capture this comparison without assigning a reversed learning order.

record.verdict_notes: There are no existing rows to fix. The assertion that the paper reports no training-loss evidence is incorrect: Figure 2(b) supplies relevant V6 evidence. Its small-learning-rate result does not by itself warrant a challenges verdict or establish reversed learning order.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not use completely random labels or report training error or test error at chance under random labeling.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed across label-noise fractions is reported.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs are tested.
Test accuracy is reported at several synthetic noise levels, but training-set fit is not reported. The study does not test noise fractions from none to all or establish a steady rise toward chance.
No random-label experiment tests whether regularization prevents fitting random labels or whether removing regularization harms generalization on true labels.
The study does not compare learning of real and noisy labels over training.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 with 80% symmetric label noise, constant learning rate 0.1.
relationships.reason: Based on Section 3.1 and Figure 2(b), absent from the rows: clean-sample loss decreases while noisy-sample loss remains high, supporting preferential early learning of clean labels.
relationships.display_finding: Clean-sample loss decreased while noisy-sample loss remained high, indicating preferential early learning of clean labels.
